title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 19 belongs to the block on S0T_{0,4} and S0T_{0,I} with card I = 4 (previous page: 'Étude de PΣ*_I'). It is a local picture of a canonical cell decomposition of the surface attached to a map (carte), in the combinatorial setting Grothendieck later called the cartographic group (Esquisse d'un programme).

Combinatorial data (upper left of the page):
- S is the set of vertices and A the set of edges.
- r = (s,a) is a flag or 'ray', i.e. a half-edge: a vertex s together with an edge a incident to it.
- τ1 r = (s,a1) moves to the next edge a1 at the same vertex, so τ1 acts as rotation about the vertex.
- r' = τ0 r passes to the other half of the edge.
- r'' = τ1 r' = τ1τ0 r = ω(r), so ω = τ1τ0 is the face permutation; its cycles are the faces, also labelled ω and ω'.

The figure is a cylinder seen in perspective.
- Top disc V_C^ω: a cap glued in for the face ω (lettered a_ω).
- Bottom disc V_C^{ω'}: a cap for the adjacent face ω' (lettered a_{ω'}).
- Middle ring V^ω: drawn at the level of the vertices (lettered a, underlined). Each vertex s appears as a small boundary circle (a puncture blown up) with a centre point R̃_s.

Vertices (0-cells) of the decomposition:
- P̃_a^ω, P̃_{a1}^ω: points on the boundary of the face cap ω, one for each edge on that face.
- P̃_s^ω: points on the face boundary, one for each corner s of ω.
- Q̃_a, Q̃_{a1}: midpoints of edges, on the middle ring.
- R̃_r, R̃_{r1}: points on the small circle around s, one for each ray.

Edges (1-cells):
- b̃_r: from Q̃_a to R̃_r, half of the edge a cut at its midpoint.
- ã_r: arc of the vertex circle from R̃_r to R̃_{r1}, i.e. a sector of the vertex corresponding to the passage r → τ1 r.
- c̃_a^ω (also written c̃_r): vertical segment from the face boundary point P̃_a^ω down to Q̃_a. Its translate to the other face is c̃_{a1}^{ω'} = c̃_{r1}.
- d̃_s^ω (also written d̃_r): arc of the face boundary of ω between P̃_{a1}^ω and P̃_a^ω, at the corner s. On the bottom, b̃_r^{ω'} and d̃_s^{ω'} = d̃_{r1} are the analogous arcs.

2-cells: hatched polygons labelled r, r', r''. These are the 'flag cells' of a barycentric-type subdivision. Each has boundary of the form c̃ · b̃ · ã · b̃^{-1} · c̃^{-1} · d̃, and is indexed by a ray in such a way that the τ0, τ1, ω actions permute them.

The arrows (orientations of the circles, curved arrows at the caps) fix orientation conventions. The double labels (c̃_r 'ou' c̃_a^ω, d̃_r 'ou' d̃_s^ω) record the choice between indexing a cell by a ray or by an (edge, face) or (vertex, face) pair.

Purpose: to obtain an explicit, functorial CW structure, with distinguished base points, on the compact surface with boundary attached to a map. Here vertices and possibly face centres are blown up into boundary circles. The structure should yield explicit generators and relations for the fundamental groupoid with these base points. Grothendieck needed this to set up the Teichmüller groupoids T_{g,ν} and their 'S0' (oriented / stable-structure) versions, here in the genus 0, four-point case, where generators are indexed by flags and the cartographic group acts.
errors: The line 'r2 = ω^{-1}(r1) = τ0τ1 r' seems inconsistent. With ω = τ1τ0 one has ω^{-1} = τ0^{-1}τ1^{-1}, so ω^{-1}(r1) = ω^{-1}(τ1 r) = τ0^{-1} r, which equals τ0 r = r' if τ0 is an involution, not τ0τ1 r. The heavy crossings-out on this line and the next show Grothendieck was himself correcting these conventions.

Labels are used ambiguously, as is common in working sketches: c̃_r vs c̃_a^ω, d̃_r vs d̃_s^ω, d̃_{r1} vs d̃_s^{ω'}. P̃_s^ω appears at the bottom where ω' would be expected. These are notational slips rather than mathematical errors.

ideas.what: Encoding a map by rays/flags r=(s,a) with permutations τ0, τ1 and face permutation ω = τ1τ0
ideas.modern_name: Cartographic group / permutation representation of maps (rotation systems)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Heffter, Edmonds, Jacques, Tutte); cartographic group in this form Grothendieck, Esquisse (1984), developed by Jones–Singerman, Malgoire–Voisin

ideas.what: Canonical cell decomposition of the surface attached to a map, with vertices blown up to boundary circles, face caps, and flag-indexed 2-cells, used to present the fundamental groupoid with base points
ideas.modern_name: Barycentric/flag subdivision of a ribbon graph surface; ribbon-graph cell structures used for Teichmüller/mapping class groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ribbon graph decompositions: Harer, Penner, Kontsevich (1980s–90s); Teichmüller groupoid presentations: Moore–Seiberg, Bakalov–Kirillov, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions the Teichmüller tower and maps but gives no such explicit CW construction

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working sketch of a standard flag-based cell decomposition of a map's surface, with notational bookkeeping. It is interesting as evidence that by around 1978–80 Grothendieck was building Teichmüller groupoids from explicit map-indexed CW structures, ahead of later ribbon-graph work. However, the page contains no result beyond what is routine or known.
transcription_corrections: 'c̃_r on c̃_a^ω' should read 'c̃_r ou c̃_a^ω' ('ou' = 'or').
The top label is more likely 'd̃_r ou d̃_s^ω' (with crossings-out) than 'd̃_s^ω … d̃_s^ω'.
The bottom label reads 'd̃_{r1} ou d̃_s^{ω'}'.
The middle-level label is 'V' with a small superscript ω (V^ω). The circled mark at the top of the page is a page/section marker (a circled 0 or similar).
The label next to R̃_{r1} is 'R_r' (without tilde in the image).
